newsitem.title: USA: Immunex compound may slow tumor growth.
newsitem.headline: Immunex compound may slow tumor growth.

text.p: Immunex Corp said Monday the Flt-3 compound it has been testing as an immune system booster has been shown to also be effective in slowing the growth of cancer tumors in mice.
It said it will begin a formal Phase II clinical trial of Flt-3 as an anti-tumor drug.

Flt 3 ligand is a protein previously shown to increase stem cells and dendetric cells, which are central to the immune system. As such, it could potentially be used as part of a cancer treatment to strengthen the patient whose immune system has been compromised by chemotherapy.
Immunex is conducting Phase I/II clinical trials in this application.
But it was not previously known that Flt-3 ligand might have a more direct role in treating cancer by shrinking the tumors themselves, the company said.

Results of the study were published in the June 1 issue of Nature Medicine. The study found treatment with daily injections of Flt-3 ligand for 19 days caused complete regression of tumors in 38 percent of mice with chemically induced skin tumors. In other mice, it caused a "significant decrease" in the rate of tumor growth, Immunex said.
